summary: Action View: Possible XSS vulnerability in highlight helper
details:
### Impact
`ActionView::Helpers::TextHelper#highlight` substitutes each matched phrase into the `:highlighter` string without escaping it and returns the result marked HTML-safe. Because sanitizing leaves quote characters in text unescaped, a match substituted into a quoted attribute value of the highlighter, such as the `<a href="search?q=\1">` form shown in the method's documentation, could end the attribute value and add attributes to the element, possibly leading to XSS. Applications are affected when they pass a `:highlighter` that places a placeholder inside an attribute value and highlight text or phrases that a user controls. The default `<mark>\1</mark>` highlighter and the block form are not affected.

### Details
The fixed releases HTML-escape each group substituted into the `:highlighter` string, so quotes in a match are rendered as `"` and `'`. Only the numbered placeholders `\0` to `\9` are expanded; other `String#sub` replacement escapes, such as `\k<name>`, `\&` and `\\`, are left as written. A match can no longer begin on the `>` that closes a preceding tag. Escaping makes a placeholder safe as element content or inside a quoted attribute value, but not in an unquoted attribute value, a URL, JavaScript or CSS context, or an attribute whose value is HTML. See the Action View CHANGELOG for details.

### Workarounds
Use a `:highlighter` that places the matched phrase only in element content, such as the default `<mark>\1</mark>`.

### Releases
The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

Patches for those who cannot upgrade at once:
- 8.1: https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/06938194b4fd59e1d2c8ab4a781f3c1e2b763425.patch
- 8.0: https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/c796f6198837479ada13290eb8fa767b5219a58a.patch

### Credit
This issue was found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-THHUJQVO).
